title: Polyelectrolyte Complex for Heparin Binding Domain Osteogenic Growth Factor Delivery
protocol: Dissolve 200 mg of sodium alginate in 10 ml double distilled water.
Shake for 1 hour.
Store the alginate solution at 4 °C overnight.
Filter the alginate solution with a sterile 0.2 µm syringe filter.
Disinfect the electrostatic bead generator and syringe pump with 70% ethanol.
Place a glass basin with a magnetic stir bar inside the bead generator.
Set the arm electrode of the bead generator 9 cm above the basin.
Connect the electrode cable to the knurled screw 2 of the arm electrode.
Pour 80 ml of SrCl2 solution into the basin.
Load 5 ml of filtered alginate solution into the syringe and rubber tube.
After connecting the rubber tube to the arm electrode, switch on the syringe pump at 5 ml/hr for 2 min.
Switch on the encapsulator.
Set the alginate flow rate at 5 ml/hr.
Set the voltage at 5.8 kV on the encapsulator.
Discard microbeads generated during the first two minutes or the initial 0.5 ml of alginate solution.
Collect subsequent microbeads in 0.2 M strontium chloride solution.
Turn off the syringe pump after pumping the pre-planned volume of alginate solution.
Turn off the encapsulator.
Store the microbeads in 20 ml of 0.2 M strontium chloride solution at 4 °C overnight.
Collect 0.5 ml of alginate microbeads with a plastic pipette.
Place the collected microbeads on a glass slide.
View the microbeads under an optical microscope at 10X magnification.
Take ten images of the microbeads with a microscope CCD camera.
Save the images with scale bar (500 µm) in TIFF format at resolution 2,048 x 1,536.
Measure the size of the microbeads using ImageJ length tools.
Convert the microbead length from pixel to micrometer.
Draw a line across the middle of the alginate bead using the line tool.
Collect the microbeads using a 100 µm nylon strainer.
Wash the beads with double distilled water.
Transfer all the microbeads made from 0.1 ml alginate solution into a 2 ml microcentrifuge tube and cover with gauze to prevent drying.
Sterilize the microbeads by autoclaving using liquid mode (115 °C, 15 min).
Add 1.5 L of distilled water to the chamber to prevent beads from drying.
Incubate the sterile microbeads with 1 ml of 2 mg/ml protamine solution for 1 hr at room temperature.
Collect 150 µl of the protamine solution for the micro bicinchoninic acid (microBCA) test.
Wash the protamine coated microbeads twice with double distilled water.
Spin down using a bench top centrifuge at 200 x g for 3 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the water using a syringe.
Incubate protamine coated microbeads with 1 ml of 0.5 mg/ml heparin solution for 30 min.
Wash off unbound heparin from the PECs by washing twice with double distilled water.
Perform the microBCA test according to manufacturer instructions.
Add 150 µl protamine solution into a 96 well plate.
Add 150 µl microBCA working solution.
Incubate the mixture for 60 min at 60 °C.
Measure the absorbance with a spectrophotometer at 562 nm.
Use albumin solution (0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 and 200 µg/ml) as calibration standards.
Determine the protamine concentration of each unknown sample according to manufacturer's instructions.
Subtract the total amount of protamine in the coating solution before incubation from the amount remaining after incubation with microbeads to determine the protamine content.
Dissolve 4 mg toluidine blue and 20 mg sodium chloride in 0.01 N hydrochloric acid to make the working solution.
Add 400 µl of sample to the working solution at a ratio of 2:3 and vortex for 30 seconds.
Add 600 µl of n-hexane to the mixture and vortex to extract the toluidine blue heparin complex.
Aspirate 200 µl of the aqueous phase by syringe after phase separation.
Measure the amount of un-extracted toluidine blue in the aqueous phase using a spectrophotometer at 631 nm.
Prepare heparin standard solutions of 0-20 µg/ml.
Plot the 631 nm reading of each heparin standard versus heparin concentration in µg/ml.
Use the standard curve to determine the heparin concentration of each sample.
Observe the layer-by-layer structure by using a confocal microscope at 10X magnification.
Load 13.3 µl of 1.5 mg/ml of BMP-2 or NELL-1 solution on 100 µg of PEC.
Incubate PEC at 4 °C under 30 rpm shaking for 10 hr.
Immerse the microbeads in 1 ml of phosphate buffered saline (PBS) at 37 °C with constant shaking (30 rpm).
Collect 1 ml of the supernatant and replace it with 1 ml PBS after 1, 3, 6, 10 and 14 days.
Evaluate the uptake and release efficiency of BMP-2 using the ELISA method according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Evaluate the uptake and release efficiency of NELL-1 using the carboxybenzoyl quinoline-2-carboxaldehyde (CBQCA) protein assay method according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Determine cumulative release at time (t).
Cumulative release at time (t) = Release at time (t) + Previous release at time (t-1).
Plot cumulative release of BMP-2 and NELL-1 against time.
Seed 20,000 rBMSCs per well in a 24-well plate.
Allow the cells to grow for one day with 1 ml of Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM) + 10% Fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Incubate the cells at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Replace the medium with 1 ml of osteogenic medium after 24 hours.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 7 days.
Place 300 μg PEC-NELL-1 and PEC inside cell culture inserts to keep them separate from cells.
Insert TC insert into a 24 well plate for 14 days.
Aspirate 1 ml of osteogenic medium every three days using a needle placed outside the TC insert.
Replace aspirated medium with 1 ml of fresh osteogenic medium.
Determine ALP activity after 7 and 14 days following kit manufacturer's protocol.
Lyse cells with assay buffer containing 0.1% TritonX-100 at 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Scrape off adhered cells using a cell scraper.
Incubate the cell suspension at 4 °C under agitation for at least 60 minutes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 2,500 x g at 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Collect the supernatant for ALP assay.
Add 50 μl of serially diluted alkaline phosphatase standard solution to wells in a 96 well plate.
Dilute with dilution buffer.
Add 50 μl of p-nitrophenyl phosphate (pNPP) substrate solution into each well.
Mix the reagents by gently shaking the plate for 30 seconds.
Incubate the mixture for 30 minutes in the dark.
Measure the absorbance at 405 nm using a plate reader.
Calculate ALP activity using the calibration curve.
Determine protein content using the microBCA protein assay kit according to manufacturer's instructions.
Normalize the ALP activity by dividing ALP activity by protein content.
Incubate 200 mg of PEC-NELL-1 with 1 ml of DMEM + 10% FBS at 37 °C for 24 hours for the MTT assay.
Seed 2,000 rBMSCs per well (in 100 μl of DMEM with 10% FBS) in a 96-well plate and incubate for 1 day at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Replace DMEM + 10% FBS with 100 μl of PEC-NELL-1/PEC extract and incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
After 1 day or 3 days of incubation, add 10 μl of 5 mg/ml MTT solution and further incubate at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 4 hours in darkness.
Add 100 μl DMSO solution to each well to dissolve formazan crystals.
Determine the absorbance at 570 nm using a microplate reader.
Calculate the relative growth rate based on the formula provided.
Pack the PECs into the pores of a bioresorbable medical grade Polycaprolactone - tri-calcium phosphate (mPCL-TCP) scaffold using a sterilized spatula inside a BSL-2 chamber.
Mix 1.5 mg/ml solution of BMP-2 or NELL-1 with the mPCL-TCP scaffold packed with PEC.
Incubate the mixture overnight at 4°C.
